1.content:
| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Scope of Work | Bristlecone shall provide the Services described in this SOW in accordance with the governing MSA. |
| Scope Description | Services cover implementation of Google’s Silicon Customer Owned Tooling supply chain across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open for manufacturing traceability, constrained supply planning, and partner collaboration across the US, India, Taiwan, TSMC, KYEC, SPIL, Foxconn, Google Hub, Warehouse, and Google USA. In scope are AS-IS and requirements gathering for Kinaxis and SAP S/4HANA; TO-BE process finalization; SAP PP/MM configuration for silicon manufacturing; Kinaxis design and configuration for wafer and supply planning; integration design and enablement for Kinaxis-SAP, E2Open collaboration flows, and GPlan-mediated PLM/SAP/Kinaxis exchanges; material master and batch traceability setup; production planning, quality management, materials management, constrained planning with yield, and organizational change management with end-user adoption tracking and reporting. Phase 1 delivers manufacturing visibility before Thanksgiving 2026 and TSMC PO capability by December 4, 2026; Phase 2 delivers technical go-live in January 2027, full MVP by January 25, 2027, and business go-live in April 2027; Phase 3 scales expanded scope from April through December 2027, including international mid-stream flows as approved for that phase. Integration and planning design shall support silicon-specific data growth, scenario structures, and new data-source setup required for the Google ecosystem. |

1.3.content:
- Material valuation, costing, yield accounting, TMS, EWM, and Commercial Invoice APIs are handled by Google Corp Eng/ASCII or are out of scope for Bristlecone.
- BOM explosion and GPN/BOM sharing from PLM can be leveraged from the current SAP landscape and consumed by Kinaxis.
- TSMC PO capability must be live by December 4, 2026, and the 22-week fab runway governs upstream readiness.
- Google owns WIP only after probe completion at TSMC; ownership transfers at goods receipt.
- Phase 1 and Phase 2 manufacturing steps occur within Taiwan, with no international mid-stream flows until Phase 3.
- Inventory POs will be issued to TSMC and UMTC for wafer and substrate procurement, and subcontracting POs will be issued to OSATs for transformation steps.
- GPlan remains the primary middleware between PLM, SAP, and Kinaxis, and Google’s internal team configures that integration layer.
- If any assumption does not hold, the Change Request process in section 5 applies and cost or timeline may be revised.

1.4.content:
- CO/FICO configuration is not included and remains with Google’s internal team.
- Material valuation, costing, and yield accounting are not included.
- TMS, EWM, and Commercial Invoice API delivery are not included unless later approved through change request.
- Manufacturing collaboration and Silicon Data Hub net-new integrations are not included in Bristlecone scope.
- WMS and TMS services are not included.
- International mid-stream flow design and deployment before Phase 3 are not included.
- SAP GTS or external trade compliance system implementation is not included unless expressly added to scope.
- No services outside the scope expressly stated in this section are included; any additional work requires a change request.

2.1.content:
- Standard working hours are based on a 40-hour work week, Monday through Friday, excluding applicable local public holidays at the assigned service location.
- For onsite resources, the holiday calendar and standard business hours of the client location apply; for offshore resources, the holiday calendar and standard business hours of the offshore delivery location apply.
- Hybrid teams will coordinate a common collaboration window across US, India, and Taiwan to support project delivery, governance forums, and issue resolution.
- Work requested outside standard working hours, on weekends, or on applicable local public holidays will be performed only with prior client approval and will be charged at the agreed role rates plus any approved shift allowance or overtime premium set out in the Commercials section.
- Time worked outside standard hours remains billable on actual effort expended against approved timesheets and does not convert the engagement to milestone-based or deliverable-based billing.

2.2.content:
- Service Location: Hybrid.
- Delivery will be performed across onsite and offshore locations, with primary delivery from the United States and India and execution support across Taiwan for business, partner, and deployment activities.
- The expected delivery split is approximately 30% onsite/client-facing and 70% offshore/remote, subject to phase needs, workshops, go-live support, and client direction.
- Named delivery locations include Google USA, India, and Taiwan, with project coordination involving TSMC, KYEC, SPIL, Google Hub, and Warehouse locations as required by the in-scope process and integration activities.
- Temporary changes to the location mix for workshops, cutover, hypercare, or issue resolution will be managed through project governance and billed on a time-and-materials basis at the agreed rates, with travel and related expenses handled under the Travel & Expenses terms.

3.content:
Deliverables submitted by Bristlecone will be reviewed by Google against the applicable measurable acceptance criteria defined for that deliverable in the SOW, including approved test evidence, documented outputs, and completion of the agreed scope for the relevant phase. Review and acceptance are for confirming quality, completeness, and conformity to the stated acceptance criteria only and do not control billing, invoicing, or payment, which will follow the Time & Materials model set out in the Commercials section.

For each deliverable, Google will identify the designated reviewer in the applicable deliverables schedule, and the review window will be stated there as an explicit number of Business Days or Calendar Days from delivery submission. A rejection must be issued in writing within that review window and must identify the specific acceptance criterion not met, with reasonable supporting detail.

If Google rejects a deliverable within the review window, Bristlecone will correct the identified non-conformities and re-submit the deliverable for re-review. Each re-submission will be reviewed against the same acceptance criteria within the same stated review window unless otherwise agreed in writing.

Absent a written rejection naming the failed criterion within the review window, the deliverable is deemed accepted automatically on expiry of that review window.

5.content:
Any change to the agreed scope, assumptions, deliverables, delivery approach, resourcing, delivery locations, dependencies, interfaces, schedule, or not-to-exceed ceiling will be handled only through the formal Change Request process. Each Change Request must describe the requested change and include a mandatory impact assessment covering commercials and timeline, quantified in all cases, including where the conclusion is zero cost impact and/or zero schedule impact.

| Step | Activity | Owner | Turnaround |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Raise Change Request with description of the proposed change, business rationale, affected scope, and requested effective date | Requesting Party | 2 business days from identification of the change |
| 2 | Log the Change Request, assign a tracking ID, and confirm completeness of submission | Bristlecone Program Manager | 1 business day from receipt |
| 3 | Prepare impact assessment covering scope, effort, commercials, timeline, dependencies, risks, and assumptions; quantify the commercial and timeline impact even if nil | Bristlecone Program Manager with relevant workstream leads; Google Project Manager to provide client-side impact inputs as needed | 5 business days from logging |
| 4 | Review the impact assessment, clarify open points, and confirm whether the Change Request is accepted, rejected, or returned for revision | Bristlecone Engagement Manager and Google Project Manager | 3 business days from impact assessment submission |
| 5 | Approve and sign the Change Request or related SOW amendment/addendum | Bristlecone Engagement Manager and Google Project Manager; final commercial approval authority: <CONFIRM: named approval role on each side if different from project roles> | 3 business days from review completion |
| 6 | Implement the approved change, update the project plan and controlled scope baseline, and close the Change Request record | Bristlecone Program Manager | 2 business days from full approval and signature |

No work related to a Change Request will begin until the Change Request, and any required SOW amendment or addendum, is approved and signed by both parties. Work performed before that approval is not chargeable and will not justify any extension, re-baselining, or movement of an agreed date.

Approved Change Requests will be incorporated into the SOW, project plan, and not-to-exceed ceiling as applicable. Rejected or withdrawn Change Requests will have no contractual effect. Payment remains on a Time & Materials basis against actual effort expended at agreed rates, invoiced monthly in arrears against client-approved timesheets, and is not triggered by Change Request approval or deliverable acceptance.
